scope: Read-only source ownership and bounded-retention audit, plus the separately tested retirement-result correction. No new browser or heap profiling was performed for this receipt.

enduranceVersion.note: The running two-hour browser loaded the earlier host and CSS. It does not qualify the final two corrections; focused tests and separate browser receipts do.

confirmedFinding.before: The page-owned retirement promise resolved to Promise.allSettled results containing the previous retirement result. Each retirement retained another nested result array, creating unbounded bookkeeping history over successive scenes and modal closes.
confirmedFinding.after: Promise.allSettled([...]).then(() => undefined) preserves completion and rejection isolation while discarding settled result values.
confirmedFinding.ownershipPreserved: All owned cleanup attempts still run independently. The host keeps the same barrier across close/reopen and waits before preparing either Solo or a native scene; a cleanup deadline does not authorize mounting over the unresolved old renderer.
confirmedFinding.limits: This finding establishes an unbounded result-history retention path, not that retired graphics assets were retained by those result values or that this history explains the observed process RSS.

ownedResourceRetirement.finding: Input, renderer and player each receive cleanup through allSettled; the surface and tracked owner are removed afterward. Canceled late scene/fork results are also disposed.

Player, picture, painter, actor lease and presentation lease are independently retired. Late-acquired assets join the same host retirement barrier. Its local cleanup result chain is bounded by this fixed set of scene owners, unlike the corrected page-lifetime history.
Painter disposal invalidates layers, cancels pending artwork, releases image/enemy leases and resets retained presentation state. View reset drops its last-paint and context references.
Demo board rendering disables the document-wide terrain cache. Disposal shrinks the canvas to 1×1 and removes it.
Adapter removes its canvas and abort listener. Native renderer clears registered scene resources, disposes Three renderer resources and requests context loss.
Adapter awaits renderer destruction before artwork/surface release. Native renderer removes listeners, waits for Phaser DESTROY, disposes its atlas, clears texture/frame maps and drops current state.

boundedRetainedData.bound: One immutable next payload slot; replacing or clearing it aborts its predecessor. It does not prepare a second world or renderer.

Each finite authored Journey source retains its latest compiled entry/level after admission; at most the current 139 built-in Journey source identities, rather than a new entry per rotation. This retained source data is not an active renderer.
Adapter retains its latest player/proof reference plus imported modules, replacing that reference on the next SIM source. Disposed physics ownership is distinct from retained replay/state data.
Page-owned actor image reservations are capped at 64MiB, or 32MiB for the compact pool, including unfinished decodes. Leases release entries when decoding settles.
Legacy painter images have a 16×1024×1024-pixel retained/reserved budget; painter board layers have a 4×1024×1024-pixel allocation budget at line571.
Shared enemy image pool admits at most 7 entries; scene leases are released on painter disposal.
Diagnostics retain at most 128 entries with bounded message/stack strings. The paused originating game and shared host display canvas intentionally remain owned by their normal page.

focusedTests.command: node --test --test-concurrency=1 game/test/demo-native-host.test.mjs game/test/demo-shared.test.mjs game/test/demo-director.test.mjs game/test/demo-solo-adapter.test.mjs game/test/demo-loading-host.test.mjs

specificRegressions.result: Quick close/reopen cannot mount a second renderer until old async cleanup resolves; the completed barrier resolves to undefined.
Six close/reopen cycles with throwing renderer disposal still retire every player, remove every surface and resolve cleanup to undefined.
Async replacement, independent cleanup after synchronous/asynchronous errors, and late assets following cancellation all pass.
Replacement and fallback both await asynchronous cleanup; total recovery deadline tests also pass.

postBarrierBrowser.note: Separate Chromium interaction/resource retirement check after the barrier correction and before the CSS centering correction; not a second two-hour run.

finalLayout.note: Final CSS verified separately in Chromium: Snake, SIM and Survival at 390×844 and 1280×800, centered visible canvases, no overflow, accessible controls, no page errors.

verification.formatChecks: Focused host/director changes passed lint, formatting and diff checks when released. Final CSS passed Prettier and both demo-layout tests.

observationsAvailableAtReview.note: Coarse resident-set snapshot; shared pages can be counted more than once. Collection starts during the run, not at process launch.

coarseProcessObservations.interpretation: These snapshots were collected approximately 44 and 58 minutes into the pre-correction run, not from process launch. The file may gain later observations. Values are RSS observations, not final maxima or exact JavaScript heap/GPU allocation measurements; shared pages may be counted more than once.

limitations: The inspected cleanup paths and focused tests support resource ownership claims, but do not prove that the complete application, browser or graphics driver has no memory leak.
Decoded assets, finite source catalogs, the paused origin, browser caches and garbage-collection timing can contribute to working-set size independently of active demo scene counts.
Observed renderer/worker/practice counters cover registered owners. Worker termination requests do not prove immediate native thread exit, and unknown GPU/browser allocations are not zero.

No initial RSS baseline, forced-GC heap comparison, allocation timeline or exhaustive third-party native-memory audit was available. The coarse snapshots alone support neither a leak diagnosis nor a no-leak conclusion.
